turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

turns.doctor_question: Have there been any specific changes, stressors, or events in your life recently that seem to be connected to when these outbursts started happening?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, there was. It all started about three weeks ago. We had a... well, there was a valve failure at the facility, and it led to an injury on the floor. Ever since that happened, I've just been like this. So, yeah, it's been going on for right around three weeks now.

turns.doctor_question: Since the incident at work, have you noticed that your anger or irritability has been ongoing, even when there isn’t a specific trigger or stressor happening at the moment?

I'll be on a normal operations call and just start snapping at my team, or I'll be sitting at home and do the exact same thing to my family. It's just... always there right now, constantly under the surface. And like I said, that is really not how I've ever handled things in the past.

symptom_reasoning.S077: The patient confirms ongoing irritability and angry outbursts without provocation, describing blowing up and snapping at coworkers and family.

turns.doctor_question: Since this started, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I guess so. I don't know if "hopeless" is the right word, but I definitely can't seem to feel good about things anymore. 

Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will talk about soccer like normal... and I know I should feel glad to just be sitting there with them. I really should. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond right now. I just can't feel happy about it.

symptom_reasoning.S076: The patient explicitly describes an inability to feel happy, glad, or emotionally responsive during meaningful family interactions, clearly demonstrating an inability to experience positive emotions.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me more about the valve failure and the injury? Did you feel personally affected by it, or has it been haunting you in any way since it happened?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, it's definitely been haunting me. I didn't get hurt myself, but I was right there when it happened. 

And now... it just won't leave me alone. I can be sitting at the kitchen table, or just trying to answer some emails from home, and suddenly I'm right back there. I see the flash from the valve failing, I see the smoke filling up the aisle... it just shoves everything else out of my head. It's like I'm watching it happen all over again, and I can't stop it.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient describes involuntary, distressing re-experiencing and vivid intrusive memories/flashbacks of the traumatic event that shove everything else out of their head.

turns.doctor_question: Since the incident with the valve failure, have you noticed any physical reactions—like a fast heartbeat, sweating, or shaking—when something reminds you of what happened?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart isn't racing, and I'm not sweating or shaking or anything. It's just the images in my head, but my body feels pretty normal, I guess. I haven't had any physical reactions like you're describing.

turns.doctor_question: Since the valve failure incident, have you had trouble sleeping or staying asleep, especially because of thoughts or images related to what happened?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, my sleep has been pretty terrible. Most nights I just lie there in bed, and I keep hearing that alarm going off in my head. By the time morning actually comes around, I feel like I never slept at all.
